t.3.52.1: But Vaidehī, as she was being carried away and saw no protector anywhere, beheld five bull-like monkeys standing on a mountain peak.
t.3.52.2: In their midst the large-eyed, fair-hipped Maithilī let fall her golden-hued silken upper garment and her lovely ornaments, thinking that they might tell Rāma.
t.3.52.4: Then the tawny-eyed bulls among the monkeys saw that large-eyed Sītā crying out aloud, gazing at her as if with unblinking eyes.
t.3.52.3: Casting off her garment together with her ornaments, she let it fall into their midst; but Daśagrīva, in his haste and agitation, did not notice that deed.
t.3.52.5: And he, the lord of the rākṣasas, having passed beyond Pampā and seizing the weeping Maithilī, went on toward the city of Laṅkā.
t.3.52.6: Rāvaṇa, greatly delighted, carried her off upon his lap, carrying his own death, as one would carry on his lap a she-serpent with sharp fangs and deadly venom.
t.3.52.7: Through the sky he swiftly passed beyond forests, rivers, mountains and lakes, like an arrow loosed from a bow.
t.3.52.8: Reaching the ocean, the home of whales and crocodiles, the inexhaustible abode of Varuṇa, the refuge of rivers, he passed beyond it.
t.3.52.9: While Vaidehī was being carried off, the ocean, abode of Varuṇa, in its agitation had its waves tossed about and its fish and great serpents held motionless.
t.3.52.10: Then the Cāraṇas sent forth words that rang through the sky, and the Siddhas then declared, "This is the end of Daśagrīva!"
t.3.52.11: But Rāvaṇa, holding the writhing Sītā on his lap, entered the city of Laṅkā, carrying her who was his own death in embodied form.
t.3.52.13: There Rāvaṇa placed Sītā, she of the dark-cornered eyes, wholly given over to grief and bewilderment, just as Maya laid down his demonic illusion.
t.3.52.12: Having reached the city of Laṅkā, with its well-laid-out highways, he entered his own inner apartments, abounding in crowded courtyards.
t.3.52.14: And Daśagrīva said to the fearsome-looking piśācīs: "See to it that no man or woman looks upon this Sītā without my consent."
t.3.52.15: Pearls, gems and gold, garments and ornaments, whatever she may desire, that very thing is to be given to her, just as if it were my own wish.
t.3.52.16: And whichever woman speaks even the slightest unpleasant word to Vaidehī, whether through ignorance or knowingly, does not hold her life dear.
t.3.52.17: Having spoken thus to those rākṣasīs, the mighty lord of the rākṣasas went out from that inner apartment, pondering what ought to be done, and he saw eight rākṣasas of great valour who fed on raw flesh.
t.3.52.18: Seeing them, that mighty one, deluded by the boon he had been granted, praised them for their strength and valor and spoke these words to them.
t.3.52.19: O you who bear various weapons, go quickly from here, with all haste! Janasthāna, which was formerly the abode of Khara, is now a place laid waste.
t.3.52.21: For that very great army of mine which was stationed in Janasthāna, together with Khara and Dūṣaṇa, has been slain in battle by the arrows of Rāma.
t.3.52.20: Let your dwelling be there in Janasthāna, now empty, its rākṣasas slain, relying on your manly strength and casting fear far away.
t.3.52.22: Then an unprecedented anger rises in me, overwhelming my composure, and a very great and most terrible enmity has arisen toward Rāma.
t.3.52.23: I wish to exact that vengeance from my enemy, for I shall find no sleep until I have slain the foe in battle.
t.3.52.24: But now, having slain that Rāma, the slayer of Khara and Dūṣaṇa, I shall find peace, like a pauper who has gained wealth.
t.3.52.26: All you night-wanderers must go forth with vigilance, and you must ever strive toward the slaying of Rāghava.
t.3.52.25: You who dwell in Janasthāna must bring me accurate news concerning Rāma, telling me truly what he is doing.
t.3.52.27: For I know your strength, having seen it many times at the forefront of battle; and that is why I have appointed you here in Janasthāna.
t.3.52.28: Then the eight rākṣasas, having received those pleasing words of great import, saluted Rāvaṇa, left Laṅkā together, and set out toward Janasthāna, their forms invisible to the eye.
t.3.52.29: Then Rāvaṇa, having gained Sītā, was overjoyed; seizing the Maithilī and having kindled the gravest enmity with Rāma, that Rākṣasa rejoiced in his delusion.
